issues.display_title: Issue #417: DB: Personalization Onboarding migration — user_detail columns (CockroachDB)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 30/07/26

✅ Implementation: Personalization Onboarding user_detail DDL

This document tracks the database changes for
panorra-api-new#417
applied to the CockroachDB development database (panorra_dev).

Changes Applied

  • Added onboarding_completed as BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false.
  • Added nullable discovery_source as STRING.
  • Added nullable place_interests as JSONB.
  • Added nullable usage_intent as STRING.
  • Added nullable onboarding_completed_at as TIMESTAMPTZ.
  • Ran each ALTER TABLE as a separate statement, following CockroachDB schema-change requirements.
  • Added user_detail_discovery_source_check to accept only the six supported discovery-source values or NULL.
  • Added user_detail_usage_intent_check to accept only the six supported usage-intent values or NULL.
  • Left place_interests without a database constraint; its array contents will be validated by the API.
  • Did not add an index because the new columns are not currently used for filtering.

CockroachDB reports STRING as text and TIMESTAMPTZ as
timestamp with time zone in information_schema.columns.

Verification

  • Queried information_schema.columns and confirmed all five columns exist with the expected types, nullability, and defaults.
  • Confirmed seven NEW SCHEMA CHANGE jobs succeeded: five column additions and two CHECK constraints.
  • Observed one SCHEMA CHANGE GC job still running with waiting for MVCC GC. This is normal asynchronous cleanup and does not block use of the new schema.

Verification queries:

SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'user_detail'
  AND column_name IN (
      'onboarding_completed',
      'discovery_source',
      'place_interests',
      'usage_intent',
      'onboarding_completed_at'
  )
ORDER BY column_name;
SELECT job_id, job_type, status, description, created, finished, error
FROM [SHOW JOBS]
WHERE job_type IN ('NEW SCHEMA CHANGE', 'SCHEMA CHANGE GC')
ORDER BY created DESC;

Status

  • Development schema: completed.
  • CHECK constraints: applied.
  • Existing-user backfill: not yet decided or applied.
  • Other environments: not yet recorded as applied.

Notes

  • DDL source: docs/tasks/2026-07-30/417_personalization_onboarding_ddl.sql.
  • Decide whether existing users remain onboarding_completed = false or are backfilled to true before release.
  • Apply and verify the DDL in each remaining environment before deploying the write and read APIs.
  • If Hasura still uses this database, track the new columns and configure the required permissions.
  • API write and read changes are outside this migration and are tracked by panorra-api-new#416 and panorra-api-go#471.

Database migration for the Personalization Onboarding flow specified in panorra-pwa#3223 (formerly named "KYC").

This blocks both code tasks. Run it first:

  • Write API — #416
  • Read API — GoThruMedia/panorra-api-go#471

The database is CockroachDB. The DDL below follows CockroachDB semantics, which differ from PostgreSQL in ways that matter here — the notes explain where and why.

There is no migration tooling in either repo: no migrations directory, no AutoMigrate, no Migrator(). ansible-deploy.yml only builds the binary and restarts pm2, it never touches the database. Schema changes are applied out of band — see open question 1.

1. Add the columns

ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD COLUMN onboarding_completed    BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD COLUMN discovery_source        STRING;
ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD COLUMN place_interests         JSONB;
ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD COLUMN usage_intent            STRING;
ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD COLUMN onboarding_completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

Run these as five separate statements, not one combined ALTER TABLE. CockroachDB permits the combined form but does not guarantee its atomicity:

The limitation on transactional schema changes also applies to single ALTER TABLE statements that include multiple schema modifications.

If a combined statement fails on the third column, you cannot tell whether the first two landed without checking manually. Separate statements fail independently and are individually re-runnable.

Do not wrap these in BEGIN / COMMIT. From the CockroachDB docs:

Most schema changes should not be performed within an explicit transaction with multiple statements. Execute schema changes either as single statements (as an implicit transaction), or in an explicit transaction consisting of the single schema change statement.

Each ADD COLUMN is an asynchronous job, not an instant metadata edit. PostgreSQL 11+ optimises ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT false into a metadata-only change; do not assume CockroachDB does the same. It runs an online schema change that backfills rows — non-blocking, but real work proportional to table size. Wait for each one before running the next:

SHOW JOBS WHERE job_type = 'SCHEMA CHANGE';

Column choices

column type rationale
onboarding_completed BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false Read on every page load for the redirect decision. Making it nullable would force the frontend to handle three states when it only needs two.
discovery_source STRING nullable NULL means unanswered, which is distinct from ''.
place_interests JSONB nullable An array of 1–8 strings. Follows the existing location column, already json.RawMessage in UserDetail.go:27.
usage_intent STRING nullable Same reasoning as discovery_source.
onboarding_completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ nullable Check whether the existing created_at / updated_at columns use TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ and match them.

STRING is CockroachDB's alias for TEXT; either spelling works.

Why not a native array type for place_interests: GORM does not handle Postgres arrays without pq.StringArray or a custom type. JSONB with json.RawMessage works as-is and the pattern already exists on this table.

Why not a join table against categories: §15 of the spec defines eight fixed string enums, not IDs. Categories holds post categories — a different domain. A join table for eight constant values costs one table plus a join on every read and buys nothing.

Why not a SQL ENUM type: adding a value later requires ALTER TYPE. Plain strings with application-level validation are easier to evolve.

2. CHECK constraints (recommended — see open question 4)

ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS user_detail_discovery_source_check
  CHECK (discovery_source IS NULL OR discovery_source IN (
    'social_media','friend_or_family','search_engine',
    'blog_or_article','event_or_community','other'));

ALTER TABLE user_detail ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS user_detail_usage_intent_check
  CHECK (usage_intent IS NULL OR usage_intent IN (
    'explore_virtually','find_near_me','plan_trip',
    'discover_hidden_gems','preview_venue_property','upload_share_360'));

CockroachDB validates existing data when a CHECK constraint is added, and the statement fails if any row violates it. That is safe here: every existing row is NULL, and IS NULL OR ... admits it, so this runs instantly. IF NOT EXISTS keeps it re-runnable.

The point is defence against writers that are not the API — support tooling, manual scripts, anything with SQL access. Application validation does not cover those, and a typo written directly to the table would quietly poison the recommendation data.

No CHECK on place_interests: validating array contents inside a constraint expression produces something nobody will want to read. Application-level validation is enough there.

Trade-off: adding an option later means DROP CONSTRAINT then ADD CONSTRAINT. Fast, but an extra step. If the option list is expected to churn, skip this section.

3. Index — not yet

When the recommendation feature starts querying these columns:

CREATE INDEX ON user_detail USING GIN (place_interests);

No CONCURRENTLY — all CockroachDB schema changes are online by default, the keyword is not needed.

GIN indexes on JSONB in CockroachDB support @>, <@ and = (the last via ->), which covers the eventual query shape:

SELECT user_id FROM user_detail WHERE place_interests @> '["nature_scenery"]';

Right now nothing reads these columns for filtering — they are only fetched per-user via user_id, which is already indexed. A GIN index today is write cost with no reader. Defer it.

4. Backfill (see open question 3)

DEFAULT false means every existing user enters the onboarding flow on their next login.

If existing accounts should be skipped, note that a single large UPDATE is the wrong approach on CockroachDB. It can exceed the transaction size limit and fail with a transaction retry or "transaction deadline exceeded" error after doing a lot of work. The documented pattern is a batched loop driven by primary key, with AS OF SYSTEM TIME to reduce contention:

-- repeat until zero rows come back
BEGIN;
SET TRANSACTION AS OF SYSTEM TIME '-5s';
SELECT id FROM user_detail
WHERE onboarding_completed = false
  AND created_at < '<RELEASE_DATE>'
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 5000;
COMMIT;

-- then, per chunk of roughly 2000 ids:
UPDATE user_detail
SET onboarding_completed = true
WHERE id = ANY ARRAY[<id_batch>];

The onboarding_completed = false predicate makes the loop idempotent — processed batches are not picked up again.

Leave onboarding_completed_at as NULL during backfill. That keeps "genuinely completed the flow" distinguishable from "grandfathered in", which matters when measuring completion rate later.

Below roughly 50k rows a plain single UPDATE is likely fine. Above that, batch it. See open question 2.

5. Rollback

ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS user_detail_discovery_source_check;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS user_detail_usage_intent_check;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS onboarding_completed;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS discovery_source;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS place_interests;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS usage_intent;
ALTER TABLE user_detail DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS onboarding_completed_at;

One at a time, outside any transaction. CockroachDB warns that a DROP COLUMN combined with other changes can lose data if one of those changes fails or is cancelled.

This destroys data permanently. If any user has already filled the flow in, dump the columns first.

6. Verify

SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'user_detail'
  AND column_name IN ('onboarding_completed','discovery_source',
                      'place_interests','usage_intent','onboarding_completed_at');

Expect five rows.

7. Order of operations

  1. Run the five ADD COLUMN statements one at a time, waiting for SHOW JOBS between each.
  2. Verify all five columns exist.
  3. Optional: add the two CHECK constraints.
  4. Optional: run the backfill.
  5. Only then deploy the new binaries from #416 and panorra-api-go#471.

Running the ALTERs ahead of the deploy is completely safe — the columns appear, nothing reads them, the running applications do not care. The reverse is not: deploying the code first makes SaveOnboarding fail on missing columns.

Acceptance criteria

  • Five columns exist on user_detail, confirmed via the information_schema.columns query above
  • Each ADD COLUMN schema change job reached succeeded in SHOW JOBS
  • CHECK constraints added, or explicitly declined (open question 4)
  • Backfill decision made and applied, or explicitly declined (open question 3)
  • Applied to every environment the API runs against — development first, then the rest
  • Rollback SQL confirmed to work in development before touching production

Open questions

  1. How are migrations applied? cockroach sql directly, a GUI client, or something else outside the repo? There is no migration tooling in either repo.
  2. How many rows are in user_detail today? This determines how long each ADD COLUMN job takes and whether the backfill has to be batched.
  3. Backfill: are existing users skipped, or do they all get the onboarding flow? Three options: (a) no backfill, everyone sees it — full preference coverage but existing users get interrupted; (b) backfill all existing accounts to true, so only new users see it — safest, but existing users are never drawn into personalisation; (c) backfill, then offer it optionally via Profile → Preferences (§25) — needs a frontend entry point that is not in the v1 scope.
  4. Are the CHECK constraints wanted? See section 2 for the trade-off.
  5. Is Hasura still in front of this database? The auth middleware reads https://hasura.io/jwt/claims (AuthMiddleware.go:65), but there is no Hasura metadata in either repo. If Hasura still fronts the same database, the new columns need to be tracked and given permissions, or GraphQL clients will not see them.

issues.display_title: Issue #414: API Adjustment: Contact Us Form — fullname/email, subject select, multi-file attachments
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 30/07/26

✅ Implementation: Contact Us API Adjustment

This document tracks the implementation of
panorra-api-new#414,
merged through panorra-api-new#415
in commit 6f73686.

Phase 1: Contact Us Submitter and Form Validation

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ContactUs.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added guest submissions using multipart fullname and email fields.
    • Kept authenticated user data authoritative; client-supplied identity fields are ignored for logged-in users.
    • Added guest fullname checks and email validation through net/mail.
    • Accepted both message and legacy description fields.
    • Preserved the subject enum and normalized other to Other.
    • Made version optional with - as the email value when omitted.
    • Made platform optional with Panorra Web as the default while preserving pw and pm inputs.
    • Escaped user-controlled text before including it in email content.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 2: Attachment Upload

  • Target Files:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadAttachments.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Accepted uploads from the new file form field while retaining the legacy image field.
    • Allowed JPEG, PNG, PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, and TXT attachments.
    • Validated attachment types using detected file content plus the expected extension where container MIME types are ambiguous.
    • Replaced the overflow-prone int8 size calculation with a direct byte comparison against the 2 MB per-file limit.
    • Added response metadata: filename, original_filename, size, mime_type, and status while preserving u_name.
    • Allowed viewer uploads but rejected encrypted responses for viewer sessions.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 3: Contact Us Attachment Processing

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ContactUs.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Enforced a maximum of five attachments per Contact Us submission.
    • Rejected malformed entries, missing local files, invalid content, and unsupported types instead of silently dropping them.
    • Sanitized submitted filenames with filepath.Base before resolving local paths.
    • Uploaded all validated attachments to MinIO before deleting temporary local files.
    • Replaced log.Fatalln with an HTTP 500 response so an upload failure no longer terminates the API process.
    • Used original filenames as email link labels.
    • Continued using imgproxy links for images and API download links for non-image attachments.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 4: Non-Image Attachment Download

  • Target Files:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/DownloadAttachment.go
    • src/Controllers/V1/PostsController.go
    • src/Routes/V1/AdditionalRoutes.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added GET /attachment/:kind/:filename for streaming private MinIO objects through the API.
    • Restricted attachment kinds to c (Contact Us) and b (Report Bug).
    • Sanitized filenames before object lookup.
    • Returned attachment content with the stored MIME type and download filename.
    • Added a download rate limit of 60 requests per minute per client IP.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 5: Abuse Protection and Proxy Handling

  • Target Files:
    • src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go
    • src/Client/Client.go
    • src/Interfaces/Interfaces.go
    • cmd/main.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added a Contact Us rate limit of five requests per minute per client IP.
    • Enabled Fiber trusted-proxy checking unconditionally.
    • Configured X-Forwarded-For as the proxy header and passed the trusted proxy list into Fiber.
    • Prevented untrusted clients from spoofing c.IP() to bypass rate limits.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 6: Shared Report Bug Attachment Behavior

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Report/ReportBug.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Reused shared attachment type validation for Report Bug submissions.
    • Added non-image download links through the API endpoint.
    • Used submitted filenames as email labels.
    • Replaced fatal MinIO error handling with an HTTP 500 response.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Phase 7: API Collection and Tests

  • Target Files:
    • api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Contact Us/Contact Us.yml
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ContactUs_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/DownloadAttachment_test.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/attachments_test.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Updated the Bruno request with fullname, email, message, optional version and platform, and attachment metadata.
    • Added tests for subject and platform normalization.
    • Added tests for download filename sanitization.
    • Added tests for supported attachment MIME and extension mappings.
  • Status: Completed and merged.

Verification

  • Reviewed merge commit 6f73686 and all 17 changed files from PR #415.
  • Confirmed the pull request was merged into development on July 30, 2026.
  • A fresh package test command was started for the affected packages but did not finish within the 120-second verification window; no passing test result is claimed here.

Notes

  • Guest Contact Us submissions are enabled and protected by IP rate limiting.
  • Final limits are five attachments per submission and 2 MB per file.
  • Drag-and-drop UI and per-file upload progress remain frontend responsibilities.
  • Issue #414 remains open on GitHub even though PR #415 is merged; close it after acceptance verification if no additional work remains.

Context

The new Contact Us form (web) adds fields and attachment behaviour the current API does not support. Two endpoints need adjustment:

  • POST /contact-us — src/Action/V1/Users/ContactUs.go, routed at src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go#L38
  • POST /attachment — src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadAttachments.go, routed at src/Routes/V1/AdditionalRoutes.go#L17

New form layout: Full name*, Email*, Subject* (select), Message*, Attachments (drag & drop, up to 5 files, images / PDFs / documents).

Requirements

1. fullname and email as request fields

The form now submits fullname and email explicitly. When the request carries a valid session, the API must resolve both from the logged-in user data instead of trusting the client payload; when there is no session, take them from the body.

  • Accept fullname and email in the multipart body.
  • Logged in → override with userData["fullname"] / userData["email"] (already read via UserFunctions.UserDatas at ContactUs.go:22). Client-supplied values must not win over session values.
  • Not logged in → validate fullname (non-empty) and email (format check) from the body.
  • Decide and document whether guest submissions are allowed. Current code hard-rejects with 401 at ContactUs.go:23-25; the new form has both fields as user-editable inputs, which implies guests are allowed. If guests are allowed, the 401 gate must be removed and rate limiting / anti-abuse added in its place.

2. subject — select option, no side-effect action

Subject stays a server-validated enum, purely a label carried into the notification email. No behaviour branches off it.

  • Current mapping at ContactUs.go:51-61: feature → Feature Request, performance → Performance, software → Software/Hardware Compatibility, other → (passed through unchanged — bug: it stays lowercase other in the email subject, should render as Other).
  • Confirm the final option list with the web team and expose it so the dropdown and the API cannot drift apart.
  • Unknown value → keep the 422 rejection.

3. version and platform should not be hard-required

ContactUs.go:38-40 requires version and platform on every request, and ContactUs.go:42-49 rejects anything that is not pm / pw with 422. The new web form does not collect either field.

  • Make both optional, or default platform to pw for web submissions.
  • Keep the mobile app's existing pm / pw + version payload working — this is a backward-compatible change, not a removal.

4. Attachments — multiple files, more types

POST /attachment (upload endpoint):

  • Currently accepts a single file under the form key image (UploadAttachments.go:30) and rejects any MIME type other than image/jpeg, image/jpg, image/png (UploadAttachments.go:59-61). Extend the allowed set to PDF and common document types (pdf, doc/docx, xls/xlsx, txt — confirm the final list).
  • Validate by sniffed MIME type, not by filename extension. Functions.DetectMimeType is image-oriented; it needs a non-image path for documents.
  • Size cap is currently 2MB (UploadAttachments.go:49-51) and is computed with int8(...) — a file over 127MB overflows and passes the check. Fix the cast and set the final per-file limit.
  • Enforce a max file count per submission (mockup shows 0/5). The upload endpoint is one-file-per-call, so the count check belongs in /contact-us.
  • Response should keep returning u_name plus enough metadata for the UI to render the uploaded file list (original filename, size, mime type, status).

POST /contact-us (consumer):

  • attachments is a JSON string of [{"u_name": "..."}] (ContactUs.go:63-76). Files that are missing on disk or not jpg/png are skipped silently (ContactUs.go:113-115, ContactUs.go:128-135) — the user gets a 200 and never learns their attachment was dropped. Return a validation error instead.
  • Reject when the file count exceeds the limit.
  • ContactUs.go:151-153 builds an imgproxy URL for every attachment. That only works for images — PDFs and documents need a plain object URL (presigned or direct) rather than being routed through img.panorra.com.
  • The email body currently renders links labelled Image 1, Image 2, … Use the real filename so the recipient can tell a screenshot from a PDF.

5. Bug: log.Fatalln kills the process

ContactUs.go:147 calls log.Fatalln(err) when the MinIO upload fails. That terminates the whole API process, not just the request. Must return a 500 error response.

Email template

Utils/EmailTemplate / template email_contact needs the new fullname and email from the form (rather than only the session user at ContactUs.go:27-31), and an attachment list that handles non-image files.

Acceptance criteria

  • fullname + email accepted in the body; session values take precedence when logged in
  • Guest vs. logged-in-only behaviour decided, implemented, and documented
  • subject validated against the agreed option list; other renders correctly in the email subject
  • version / platform optional; existing mobile payload still works
  • Multiple attachments accepted, up to the agreed max count
  • Images, PDFs and documents accepted; validated by sniffed MIME type
  • Per-file size limit enforced correctly (int8 overflow fixed)
  • Rejected / missing attachments produce an explicit error instead of a silent skip
  • Non-image attachments get a working (non-imgproxy) link in the email
  • log.Fatalln at ContactUs.go:147 replaced with a 500 response
  • Bruno collection updated: api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Contact Us/Contact Us.yml

Open questions

  1. Are guest (not logged in) submissions allowed? This drives whether the 401 gate stays.
  2. Final subject option list?
  3. Final allowed file types, per-file size limit, and max file count?

Note on scope

The drag-and-drop zone, the "multiple files allowed" helper text, and the per-file upload status display are frontend work. This issue covers the API contract that has to back them: multi-file upload, type/size/count validation, and per-file status in the response.

issues.display_title: Issue #410: Fix Like Post Broadcast Container and BroadcastLike Handling
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 29/07/26

✅ Implementation: Fix Like Post Broadcast Container and BroadcastLike Handling

Summary

Aligned POST /post/like broadcast container writes and GET /cronjob/broadcast-like payload handling so reused like broadcast rows refresh the queued post payload and the cronjob safely consumes nested JSON values.

Changes Applied

  • src/Action/V1/Likes/LikePost.go
    • Renamed the full queued metadata payload to vDatas to keep the type-check payload separate.
    • Marshals vDatas and dataPost once before insert/update.
    • Insert path now sets:
      • datas
      • send_data
      • created_at
      • updated_at
    • Update path now uses the matched broadcast container id.
    • Update path now refreshes:
      • datas
      • send_data
      • updated_at
    • Kept datas.type as like.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/BroadcastLike.go
    • Replaced direct . (string) assertions for nested send_data fields with shared normalization.
    • Supports decoded JSON values, legacy JSON strings, and nil values.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/BroadcastPayload.go
    • Added shared normalization used by broadcast cronjob code.

Verification

  • Ran:
go test ./src/Action/V1/Likes -count=1
  • Result:
? panorra-api-new/src/Action/V1/Likes [no test files]

Notes

This task covers the like broadcast flow only: API producer in LikePost.go and cronjob consumer in BroadcastLike.go.

Background

POST /post/like writes queued like notifications to broadcast_containers, which are later processed by GET /cronjob/broadcast-like.

The insert path stores both datas and send_data, but the update path only refreshed datas.

GET /cronjob/broadcast-like also reads broadcast_containers.send_data and needs to safely handle nested JSON fields when they are already decoded by json.Unmarshal.

Root Cause

When a like broadcast container already exists for the same sender and recipient, LikePost.go updates only the notification metadata payload. It does not refresh send_data or updated_at.

This can leave stale post payload data in the queue when the same sender likes another post before the cronjob processes the existing row.

In BroadcastLike.go, nested payload fields can be decoded JSON values, not JSON strings. Unsafe string assertions can crash the cronjob if like payload shape expands to include decoded JSON fields.

Objective

Align the like broadcast producer and consumer while keeping broadcast type as like.

Scope

  • src/Action/V1/Likes/LikePost.go
    • Keep datas.type as like.
    • Marshal datas and send_data consistently.
    • On existing row update, refresh datas, send_data, and updated_at.
    • Update by the matched broadcast container id.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/BroadcastLike.go
    • Replace unsafe nested JSON string assertions with shared normalization.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New like broadcast containers include current datas, send_data, created_at, and updated_at.
  • Existing like broadcast containers refresh send_data when reused.
  • Update uses the matched broadcast row ID.
  • Broadcast type remains like.
  • GET /cronjob/broadcast-like accepts decoded nested JSON values and legacy JSON string values.
  • Scoped verification is attempted.

issues.display_title: Issue #411: Refactor Utils UserFunctions Queries to GORM Models
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 29/07/26

✅ Implementation: Refactor Utils UserFunctions Queries

Summary

Completed the UserFunctions model-backed query refactor and fixed the SaveLogErr("0", ...) panic risk found while scanning support worker-publish callers.

Changes Applied

  • src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go
    • Added Models import.
    • Replaced CheckBlockingUser direct user_blocks lookup with Model(&Models.UserBlocks{}).
    • Replaced UpdateLastLogin direct user_detail update with Model(&Models.UserDetail{}).
    • Replaced InsertElasticContainer direct elastic_containers insert with Model(&Models.ElasticContainers{}).
    • Replaced GetBookmarksBetweenUsers direct bookmark b target with Model(&Models.Bookmark{}), preserving joins and returned ID/slug slices.
  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go
    • Updated SaveLogErr to parse UUIDs safely.
    • Preserved existing "0" system/no-user caller behavior by mapping it to the zero UUID instead of panicking.

Verification

  • Ran gofmt on modified files.
  • Ran scoped table scan:
rg -n "Config\.DB\.Table\(|\.Table\(" src\Utils\Functions\UserFunctions\UsersFunctions.go
  • Result: no matches.
  • Ran:
go test ./src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions
  • Result: passed, no test files.

Background

src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go still uses direct Table(...) calls for model-backed tables. These helpers are shared by user blocking, login metadata, ElasticSearch queueing, and bookmark cleanup flows.

Objective

Refactor model-backed UserFunctions queries to existing GORM models while preserving exported function signatures and return values.

Scope

  • CheckBlockingUser
    • Replace user_blocks table lookup with Models.UserBlocks.
  • UpdateLastLogin
    • Replace user_detail update with Models.UserDetail.
  • InsertElasticContainer
    • Replace elastic_containers insert with Models.ElasticContainers.
  • GetBookmarksBetweenUsers
    • Replace bookmark b query target with Models.Bookmark.

Constraints

  • Do not rename functions.
  • Do not change arguments or return types.
  • Preserve map keys and returned ID/slug slices.
  • Keep join behavior equivalent.

Acceptance Criteria

  • No active direct table calls remain in UsersFunctions.go.
  • SaveLogErr("0", ...) returns DB/create errors instead of panicking.
  • Scoped tests/build are attempted.

issues.display_title: Issue #412: Refactor Edit Hotspot Banner Exec Queries
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 29/07/26

✅ Implementation: Refactor Edit Hotspot Banner Exec Queries

Summary

Refactored EditHotspotBanner.go hotspot persistence to use GORM model operations instead of raw transaction Exec calls.

Changes Applied

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditHotspotBanner.go
